title: Reliance-backed Jio Platforms IPO: Will investors prefer Jio shares over RIL stock? What shareholders should know | Stock Market News
text:
Jio Platforms’ initial public offering (IPO) is scheduled to open on 21 October and close on 23 October 2026. The price band has been set at ₹1,065– ₹1,119 per share.

The issue is expected to raise around ₹30,213 crore through a fresh issue of 27 crore shares. At the upper end of the price band, Jio Platforms would be valued at approximately $108.3 billion.

The proceeds will primarily be used to repay or prepay borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm, with the remaining funds earmarked for general corporate purposes.

Following the fresh issue, Reliance Industries’ stake in Jio Platforms is expected to decline from approximately 66.43% to around 64.4%. However, RIL will retain majority control of the digital and telecom business.

Jio Platforms and Reliance Industries offer different investment propositions. Jio Platforms provides direct exposure to opportunities in telecom, digital services, cloud, and artificial intelligence. RIL, on the other hand, offers diversified exposure to energy, retail, telecom and digital businesses, according to experts.

Jio’s valuation will depend on its IPO pricing, earnings growth, subscriber monetisation, tariff increases, digital services and enterprise technology opportunities. For RIL, investors must assess the performance of its broader businesses alongside the value of its stake in Jio, according to experts.

The key consideration for investors evaluating Jio’s IPO will be whether its valuation leaves sufficient room for future returns, while RIL shareholders must weigh the benefits of diversified exposure against the potential holding-company discount.

Ratiraj Tibrewal, Director at Choice Capital, said Jio Platforms and Reliance Industries cater to different investment preferences. Jio offers more direct exposure to India’s telecom and digital services growth, backed by its large subscriber base, expanding 5G network, broadband business and emerging AI-led offerings.

At the proposed IPO valuation of 32.6 times, Jio’s investment appeal will depend on its ability to sustain earnings growth, improve monetisation and translate its scale into stronger cash flows. Investors seeking focused exposure to the digital connectivity and technology ecosystem may therefore consider Jio as a relevant addition to their portfolios, Tibrewal said.

RIL, meanwhile, offers a diversified portfolio spanning telecom, retail, oil-to-chemicals and new energy, providing exposure to multiple growth drivers through a single investment. Its stake in Jio also allows shareholders to participate indirectly in the latter’s growth.

Tibrewal said Jio’s listing could provide greater visibility into its standalone valuation and potentially influence the market’s assessment of RIL’s holding-company discount. While some investors may gravitate towards Jio for more targeted telecom and digital exposure, the choice between the two will ultimately depend on whether they prioritise focused growth or the diversification and potential value-unlocking opportunities offered by the parent company.

A ₹2,500 crore shareholder reservation has been reported for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders. However, eligibility will depend on the record date and the conditions specified in the IPO’s offer documents.

Investors should check the official offer documents for eligibility criteria before buying or selling shares under the shareholder quota. Purchasing RIL shares after the applicable record date would not establish eligibility for the reserved portion.

Ultimately, the choice between Jio Platforms and Reliance Industries will depend on investors’ preferred business exposure, valuation expectations and risk appetite. While Jio offers a more focused play on telecom and digital growth, RIL provides a diversified investment proposition with indirect exposure to Jio.

Abhinav Tiwari, Senior Research Analyst at Bonanza, said Jio Platforms’ upcoming IPO could attract strong investor interest, particularly from those seeking direct exposure to India’s expanding telecom and digital economy.

With more than 53 crore subscribers, rising data consumption, tariff hikes and growth opportunities in 5G, broadband and artificial intelligence (AI), Jio offers significant long-term growth potential, Tiwari said.

However, investor preference between Jio Platforms and Reliance Industries (RIL) will largely depend on valuations. Jio’s proposed valuation of around ₹10–11 lakh crore already factors in substantial growth expectations, potentially limiting its near-term upside.

RIL, meanwhile, offers a diversified portfolio spanning telecom, retail, energy and new energy businesses, reducing investors’ dependence on any single sector. Jio’s listing could also help unlock value for RIL shareholders.

Tiwari said growth-oriented investors may prefer Jio’s standalone telecom and digital exposure, while those seeking diversification and greater valuation comfort may continue to favour RIL. Both stocks could appeal to different investor categories.

Mohit Gulati, Managing Partner at ITI Alternatives, said the choice should not necessarily be framed as a decision between Jio and RIL. Even after the IPO, RIL is expected to retain a substantial stake in Jio, allowing its shareholders to continue benefiting from the digital business’s performance.

Gulati said the listing would give investors a choice of exposure, allowing them to invest directly in India’s telecom and digital platform businesses, separately from RIL’s oil-to-chemicals and retail operations.

He added that the IPO should not necessarily be viewed as a substitution trade. Instead, the decision should depend on how each investment fits into an investor’s portfolio, with some long-term investors potentially choosing to hold both stocks.

Saurabh Jain, Head of Fundamental Research at SMC Global Securities, said the choice between Jio Platforms’ IPO and RIL shares would depend on investors’ portfolio strategies, as both offer distinct advantages.
